free_tier.stated: 'Student awards will be up to a maximum of $5,000.00. Faculty and Staff awards are not capped.' Awards are AWS Promotional Credit, and 'Amazon EC2 usage supported by AWS Promotional Credit will be for on-demand and spot instances only'. Review cycle 90 to 120 days.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: None. The credit lands on an AWS account the applicant already holds, and the institution email is the gate that precedes the award, so no chain starts.

limits.value: the application needs an institution-issued .edu or .org address and a 90 to 120 day human review, so an unaffiliated applicant cannot submit at all.

limits_note: the application needs an institution-issued .edu or .org address and a 90 to 120 day human review, so an unaffiliated applicant cannot submit at all.
binding_note: the application needs an institution-issued .edu or .org address and a 90 to 120 day human review, so an unaffiliated applicant cannot submit at all.

identity_cost.detail: an institution-issued email address on a .edu, .org or equivalent domain, plus an eligible role at an accredited research institution (full-time faculty, full-time research staff, or an enrolled graduate/post-graduate/PhD student). The FAQ states 'Applications from non-institution domains will not be accepted.' Review takes 90 to 120 days. No card, hold, debit or prepaid term is stated: the award is credit on an AWS account the applicant already holds.

evidence.proved: 'Student awards will be up to a maximum of $5,000.00. Faculty and Staff awards are not capped' and 'Amazon EC2 usage supported by AWS Promotional Credit will be for on-demand and spot instances only' and 'Typical review cycles are 90 to 120 days', quoted; page 200

'We require applicants provide their official institution-issued email ID (.edu, .org, or equivalent) to expedite the verification and decision process. Applications from non-institution domains will not be accepted.' quoted; also 'The only exception is applications from the greater China region'
eligibility list is exactly three roles, all tied to 'an accredited research institution': full-time faculty, full-time research staff, graduate/post-graduate/PhD students enrolled there

notes: A clean refutation and the most useful negative in this class, because USD 5,000 uncapped-for-staff is the kind of number a reader would otherwise chase. Two separate gates, either of which is fatal: the .edu/.org domain rule, stated as an absolute ('will not be accepted'), and the role list, which has no independent-researcher category. The program itself is alive and global outside greater China, so the verdict is fails-identity rather than dead.
